title: Ops QuickMaps: contextual incident remediation toolkit
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build 'QuickMaps', a lightweight contextual incident remediation toolkit that converts common runbook steps into parameterized, idempotent tasks surfaced in the admin console and CLI. Goals: 1) reduce time-to-remediate for high-frequency operational incidents by surfacing context-aware suggested actions; 2) preserve auditability (RBAC, KMS-backed logs); 3) make runbook steps testable and dry-runnable in a sandbox. Scope: task authoring DSL, mapping engine that selects candidate QuickMaps based on alert context, safe execution layer with approval gating, and telemetry around success/failure/latency. Non-goals: replacing long-form playbooks or building an LLM-driven autopatcher in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Console surfaces at least three QuickMaps for target incident types (OOM, model-serve-backpressure, KV-cache-stale)
Each QuickMap executes in dry-run mode without mutating production state
Execution events are written to audit log with KMS-encrypted payloads and RBAC-checked
Telemetry dashboard shows median time-to-first-remediate reduction for test incidents
Automated tests for idempotency and permission checks included in CI
design_decisions: Use declarative YAML for QuickMap authoring to keep authoring accessible to SREs
Mapping engine will be rule-based (context predicates) in v1; LLM suggestions deferred to v2
Execution will be performed through the existing admin-runlet agent with an added sandbox flag
Approval gating integrated with existing SSO/SAML groups rather than a new permission system
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental mutation if dry-run skipped -> Mitigation: require explicit feature-flag and two-person approval for high-risk maps
Risk: sensitive data leaked in logs -> Mitigation: redact PII and store encrypted blobs in audit bucket with KMS
Risk: explosion of QuickMap variants causing maintenance overhead -> Mitigation: enforce naming conventions and introduce deprecation TTL
implementation_plan: Week 1: authoring DSL and schema, sample QuickMap catalog (YAML) and Confluence spec
Week 2: mapping engine prototype that mines alert context and matches candidate QuickMaps
Week 3: integrate sandboxed execution via admin-runlet agent and implement dry-run mode
Week 4: add RBAC checks, audit logging, KMS encryption, and CI tests
Week 5: internal dogfood on staging incidents, iterate based on operator feedback, rollout to limited beta
